sections: 21. Estimated WOZ Value (Method 2) - Example - Jan Provostlaan 16, Bilthoven

blocks.text: 19. Estimated WOZ Value (Method 2) - Process

This part describes how the Estimated WOZ Value (Method 2) is calculated for the 1,082 buildings in table method_2, the assumptions behind it, and one worked example. WOZ (Waardering Onroerende Zaken - valuation of real estate) is the Dutch property value used for local taxes.
[IMPORTANT] Model estimate, not an official WOZ value. Official WOZ values are set by municipalities; this estimate is not issued by or taken from a municipality, Kadaster or the Waarderingskamer.

Method 2 values every verblijfsobject (unit) of a building on its own and adds the values up. Dwellings and other units are valued in a different way. All buildings use the same reference year: WOZ year 2026, valuation date (waardepeildatum) 2025-01-01. The total is rounded to the nearest € 1,000.

head: Unit
Formula
rows: buurt (neighbourhood) reference value of the dwelling type x size factor x age factor
floor area x gemeente (municipality) price per m2 x location index x type factor x size factor x age factor

blocks.text: 19.1 How Method 2 differs from Method 1

head: Method 1
Method 2

Buurt (neighbourhood), corrected for the buurt's mix of dwelling types

blocks.text: 19.2 Step 1 - Split the building into verblijfsobjecten (units)

The BAG verblijfsobjecten (units) of the pand (building) are read with their oppervlakte (floor area) and gebruiksdoel (use). The 1,082 buildings contain 3,907 units; their areas add up to the BAG gebruiksoppervlakte (usable floor area, GO) of each building.
A unit with woonfunctie (residential use) of at most 400 m2 is valued as a dwelling.
A residential unit over 400 m2 (for example a care home or student housing registered as one unit) and every other unit are valued per m2.
19.3 Step 2 - Check the floor area with 3DBAG

The BAG floor area is used, as it is the area WOZ valuations use. If it is more than 2 times the BVO (bruto vloeroppervlak - gross floor area) measured from the 3DBAG building, the units are scaled down to 2 x BVO: such a difference means units of another building are registered on this one.
19.4 Step 3 - Find the buurt (neighbourhood)
PDOK Locatieserver (location server): the postcode (postal code) and huisnummer (house number) give the buurtcode (neighbourhood code), wijkcode (district code) and gemeentecode (municipality code).
If the address is not found: the postal code alone; if that fails, the gemeente (municipality) found for Method 1.
If CBS has no figures for the buurt: the wijk (district); else the gemeente (municipality).
19.5 Step 4 - Location index

A buurt with many detached houses has a high average WOZ because of its dwellings, not only because of its location. The average is therefore corrected for the buurt's mix of dwelling types before it is compared with the gemeente (municipality).
mix ratio = sum over dwelling types of (share of the type in the area x price ratio of the type)
location index = (buurt avg WOZ / buurt mix ratio) / (gemeente avg WOZ / gemeente mix ratio), limited to 0.5 - 2.

head: Source
What is used
Period
rows: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten (key figures for districts and neighbourhoods): gemiddelde WOZ-waarde van woningen (average WOZ value of dwellings) and the percentage of each dwelling type, per buurt, wijk and gemeente
Gemiddelde WOZ-waarde van woningen (average WOZ value of dwellings) per gemeente, to bring 2025 to 2026

blocks.text: 19.6 Step 5 - Dwelling type from 3DBAG geometry
The share of the building's outline that is a scheidingsmuur (party wall, shared with a neighbouring building) shows how the dwelling is built:

head: Party-wall share of the perimeter
Dwelling type
rows: Three or more dwellings, or a dwelling in a building with other uses

blocks.text: 19.7 Step 6 - Value a dwelling

buurt reference value = buurt avg WOZ (2025) x gemeente WOZ growth 2025-2026 x (price ratio of the dwelling type / buurt mix ratio). This is the expected WOZ of a typical dwelling of that type in that buurt.

size factor = (floor area / typical floor area of the type in the gemeente) ^ elasticity, with elasticity 0.9 for smaller and 0.7 for larger dwellings, limited to 0.3 - 2. The typical area of the type is scaled to the gemeente with the CBS average floor area of its dwellings.
dwelling value = buurt reference value x size factor x age factor

head: Source
What is used
Period
rows: Bestaande koopwoningen (existing owner-occupied homes): gemiddelde verkoopprijs (average sale price) per woningtype (dwelling type)
Typical floor area per woningtype (dwelling type) = gemiddelde aardgaslevering (average gas delivery) / aardgas per m2 (gas per m2)
Gemiddelde oppervlakte (average floor area) of the dwelling stock per gemeente and for the Netherlands

blocks.text: 19.8 Step 7 - Value another unit
value = floor area x gemeente (municipality) price per m2 x location index x type factor x size factor x age factor
Gemeente price per m2: CBS average WOZ of dwellings / CBS average floor area, WOZ year 2026 (as Method 1).
Type factor: the factor of the unit's own gebruiksdoel (use); a unit with several uses gets their mean.
Size factor: (floor area / 500 m2) ^ -0.1, limited to 0.6 - 1.2: larger units are worth less per m2.
19.9 Step 8 - Age factor and total
Every unit gets the age factor of the band that contains the bouwjaar (year built) of the building. The building value is the sum of its units, rounded to the nearest € 1,000.
19.10 Missing data

head: Missing input
Replaced by
rows: Postal code; else the gemeente (municipality) of Method 1
The whole building as one unit with the building's gebruiksdoel (use)
